names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 28 iulie, «Sfinții Apostoli și Diaconi Prohor, Nicanor, Timon și Parmena, dintre cei 70», with the rank words left off.

Read out of his own head line on saint.gr's page for 28 Ιουλίου, «Αγιος Παρμενας ο Αποστολος Και Διακονος», with the rank words left off; the day's listing spells it «Παρμένας». The page glosses the name from παρά and μένω, the one who remains, the steady one, the faithful friend.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's first heading for 28. јул ст. ст., „Свети апостоли: Прохор, Никанор, Тимон и Пармен.“ — «Свети» is not a rank and «апостоли» is the `apostle` the folder already carries, so what the heading leaves is the bare forename, which is all it gives any of the four. Measured before it was written: `fk.mjs` returns no other holder of this string or of anything folding to it.

hymns.text: Sfinţilor Apostoli, rugaţi pe Milostivul Dumnezeu ca să dea iertare de greşeli sufletelor noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Apostoli și Diaconi Prohor, Nicanor, Timon și Parmena, dintre cei șaptezeci», Glasul 3 — the common of apostles, as the page prints it for the four of them

english.text: Holy apostles, entreat the merciful God to grant our souls forgiveness of offences.

hymns.text: Ὡς θεῖοι συνέκδημοι, τῶν Ἀποστόλων Χριστοῦ, θεόθεν ἐκρίθητε διακονεῖν εὐσεβῶς, τῷ θείῳ πληρώματι, Πρόχορε θεηγόρε, σὺν Νικάνορι ἅμα, Τίμων ὁ θεοκήρυξ. Παρμενᾶς τε ὁ θεῖος, πρεσβεύοντες τῷ Κυρίῳ, ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — on the shared page of the four, and it names him last of them

english.text: As divine fellow travellers of the Apostles of Christ, you were judged from God to serve the divine fullness in piety — Prochorus, speaker of God, together with Nicanor, and Timon the herald of God, and divine Parmenas — interceding with the Lord for our souls.

hymns.text: Ἀπόστολοι Ἅγιοι, πρεσβεύσατε τῷ ἐλεήμονι Θεῷ , ἵνα πταισμάτων ἄφεσιν, παράσχῃ ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’ — the second hymn on the shared page of the four. It is the common of apostles and names nobody, but the page prints it under their names, so by the corpus's rule it is their service and is copied whole

english.text: Holy Apostles, intercede with the merciful God, that he may grant our souls the forgiveness of their offences.

hymns.text: Διάκονοι σεπτοί, καὶ αὐτόπται τοῦ Λόγου, καὶ σκεύη ἐκλογῆς, ἀνεδείχθητε πίστει, Νικάνορ καὶ Πρόχορε, Παρμενᾶ, Τίμων ἔνδοξε· ὅθεν σήμερον, τὴν ἱερὰν ὑμῶν μνήμην, ἑορτάζομεν, ἐν εὐφροσύνῃ καρδίας, ὑμᾶς μακαρίζοντες.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος α’, Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτὴρ — the third hymn on the shared page of the four, and it names him among them

english.text: Revered deacons and eyewitnesses of the Word, you were shown by faith to be chosen vessels, Nicanor and Prochorus, Parmenas and glorious Timon; and so today we keep your sacred memory with gladness of heart, and call you blessed.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 28 iulie — «Sfinții Apostoli și Diaconi Prohor, Nicanor, Timon și Parmena, dintre cei 70»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 28ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Πρόχορος, Νικάνωρ, Τίμων και Παρμένας οι Απόστολοι και Διάκονοι»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 28 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the four deacons are the folder's own company, with a head line each on one page. Of Parmenas the Greek page says he died at Jerusalem carrying out his deacon's work and was buried by the Apostles themselves — no martyrdom, which agrees with the folder's `types` of apostle and deacon and nothing more. The page gives no year for any of the four, so no `dates` object is proposed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. It prints three hymns and all three are taken, two of them naming him. The day's listing spells him «Παρμένας» and the hymns «Παρμενᾶς»; the stored form is the one his own head line gives.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 10.08.2026 (28. јул ст. ст.) — „Свети апостоли: Прохор, Никанор, Тимон и Пармен.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, AN ENUMERATED FOUR, so BRIEF-SERBIAN §5 counts four and each of the four folders the corpus already holds takes this one heading whole with its closing full stop; the corpus holds all four and they are already `related` to one another, so no `related` row was added anywhere. THE ENTRY SETTLES THE DAY IN ITS OWN WORDS: «А она прва четворица немају посебних дана празновања, него се сви спомињу у овај један дан, 28. јула» — these first four have no separate days of celebration but are all commemorated on this one day, 28 July. The Romanian and the Greek keep all four on this same menologion day. All four serbian rows were `undocumented`, so the rows land here. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND STILL NULL ON ALL FOUR: the entry gives not one year, naming only the apostle Peter, John the Evangelist and Patmos, and a reader does not date the apostolic age from a name. THE OTHER THREE OF THE SEVEN ARE NAMED IN THE BODY AND TAKE NOTHING: «Стефан, Филип и Николај», of whom it says that Stephen the protomartyr is kept separately on 27 December, Philip on 11 October, and «Николај није ушао у ред светитеља због своје јереси» — Nicholas did not enter the ranks of the saints because of his heresy. Membership of the Seven is not this entry's story of any one of these four, the existing `related` rows were made on the four of the heading, and a reader does not stretch a heading, so all three names stay in the book's own Cyrillic and NO ROW WAS MADE IN EITHER DIRECTION. «апостола Петра» and «св. Јована Јеванђелиста» likewise take nothing new: `john-the-theologian` is already `related` to Prochorus and no other row was touched. The Prologue prints no hymn (8 October 2026). He is the fourth name of the four, and the entry gives him one clause: «Пармен умре на очи апостола, и од ових би оплакан и погребен» — Parmenas died before the eyes of the apostles, and was mourned and buried by them. That is the whole of what this book says of him, and it agrees with this folder's `types`, which carry no `martyr`.
